sc: Infant 3–6 months in winter, cold for 2 days, then fast breathing, poor feeding, wheeze, fine crackles → Bronchiolitis (RSV)
6-week-old ex-preterm with a cold, then pauses in breathing → RSV apnoea: admit, monitor
Toddler with wheeze only with colds, well between, no atopy → Viral-induced wheeze
f: Coryza, cough, fast breathing, poor feeding · young infants: apnoea
Hyperinflation · fine crackles · wheeze · chest indrawing · hypoxia
Clinical diagnosis · pulse oximetry · X-ray only if severe or doubt
Supportive: oxygen if SpO2 < 90%, NG feeds, nasal suction · no salbutamol, no steroids, no antibiotics
Nirsevimab or palivizumab (high-risk) · maternal RSV vaccine from 28 weeks
Asthma (atopy) · heart failure (big liver, murmur) · CF (poor growth) · reflux aspiration · foreign body (one side)
trap: Bronchiolitis is RSV; croup is parainfluenza · salbutamol and steroids do not help bronchiolitis · severe adenovirus bronchiolitis → bronchiolitis obliterans
